name: DicePool Lab
idea: No-code visual calculator that gives exact odds for custom tabletop dice mechanics (success pools, push/reroll, exploding, keep/drop, roll-under opposed rolls, mixed results).
description: A GM or game designer builds a roll from blocks (pool size, success threshold, push once, explode on max, drop N failures, roll-under vs opposed) and instantly sees exact probability tables such as 'at least 2 successes with N dice, pushed or not', plus a side-by-side comparison of two characters. Results are shareable by link and printable for a GM screen. Hard to copy because the engine has to get stateful mechanics exactly right (push re-rolls, die-vs-die elimination, bounded explosions, crit-on-match) and ship presets for real systems, while the incumbent AnyDice needs its own scripting language.
web_delivery: Pure client-side SPA on Vercel hobby (TypeScript exact-distribution engine, config encoded in the URL); Supabase free only for optional saved presets.
why_hard_to_copy: Correctness-critical probability engine for mechanics that generic dice roller libraries do not model, plus a curated library of system presets (Year Zero, Blades-style, d100 roll-under, etc.).

signals.summary: A designer hacking together a d100 roll-under game asks how to compute the odds of opposed rolls (both succeed, both fail, crits) and how a skill gap shifts them; no tool answers it directly.
Someone helping a friend's homebrew (roll N d6, all must meet a bar, a drop modifier forgives failed dice) cannot get the AnyDice code right and wants an accurate probability calculator.
A Vaesen player has the book's one-success table but cannot work out the odds for two or more successes with the push-the-roll rule (re-roll everything that is not a 6).
A designer wrote a long AnyDice script to compare a plain pool against a pool that re-rolls 1s and explodes 6s with a matching/elimination step, and is unsure it is right.
Asks for the outcome odds of a Blades-in-the-Dark-like pool with mixed success on 4, full success on 5-6 and crits on matching dice, for 1 to 4 dice.
Wants a free web or app tool that computes and plots the exact probability distribution of compound dice formulas (not simulation), ideally with arbitrary precision and moments.
A user stuck on AnyDice's scripting syntax (cannot define a variable from a function result), showing the learning-curve pain of the incumbent.

competitors_seen.name: AnyDice
competitors_seen.note: Free, exact distributions, but you must learn its own scripting language; no visual builder, no built-in push or opposed-roll helpers.

competitors_seen.name: Icepool
competitors_seen.note: Powerful Python library (Pyodide web apps exist) but requires coding.

competitors_seen.name: Contract RPG dice pool calculator
competitors_seen.note: Single-system calculator with fixed rules.

satellite.name: System odds pages
satellite.what: One static page per popular dice system (Year Zero / Vaesen push odds, Blades-style pools, d100 roll-under) with the engine preloaded.
satellite.why_shared: Same engine, long-tail search traffic from players asking 'chance of at least 2 successes with N dice'.
satellite.handoff: 'Customize this roll' button opens DicePool Lab with the config in the URL.

ENWorld and GiantITP forums dice-math threads
itch.io TTRPG game-jam and devlog communities
Discord servers of indie TTRPG designers

marketing.funnel: Search or forum answer -> preset odds page -> custom builder -> shareable link that other designers open
marketing.cold_outreach: Message creators of small Year Zero / Blades hacks on itch.io offering a ready-made odds table for their core roll.
post_ideas: Exact odds of the Vaesen push mechanic for 1-10 dice (table)
Why 'roll under, both succeed' opposed d100 rolls favour the higher skill more than you think

notes: Strongest demand cluster in my sweep: six independent RPG.SE questions in about nine months plus a softwarerecs request. Doubt: a free tool for hobbyists has weak direct monetization (ads, donations, or a pro tier for saved/shared systems). AnyDice is the entrenched incumbent, so the wedge is no-code plus push/opposed/mixed-result blocks.

name: Round Night
idea: Zero-signup live tournament runner for casual offline events (Swiss and multi-player table pods) with a public screen that updates in real time.
description: An organizer types player names and gets correct pairings every round (no repeat opponents, byes, late arrivals, mid-event withdrawals, changing the round count on the fly), players report their own results from their phones, and a projector page updates standings instantly without reloads. Aimed at chess clubs, board-game cafes, table-tennis clubs and card-game store nights. Hard to copy because pairing edge cases (odd counts, late entries, repeat avoidance, 3-4 player pods) need real rules knowledge and the live-sync flow has to be dead simple.
web_delivery: Next.js or SvelteKit on Vercel hobby; Supabase free Realtime channels for the live standings page and player result entry via a join code; pairing engine in TypeScript.
why_hard_to_copy: Correct Swiss/pod pairing with late entries and withdrawals (bbpPairings-level edge cases) plus reliable real-time sync during an event; casual organizers will not forgive a bad pairing.

signals.summary: An experienced offline-tournament organizer says existing tools (Challonge and others) lag mid-event, force long forms, need page reloads for the live screen, and make withdrawals or changing the round count hard; wants one-click creation, live pairings on a screen and player self-reported results.

A table tennis club captain and referee released a free open-source desktop tournament manager because existing options did not fit; it is desktop-only (Linux/Windows/macOS), offline and needs no account, leaving the web/phone side open.

name: BackSide
idea: In-browser tool that pairs the front and back scans of old prints into one record with a caption, written as standard XMP/EXIF metadata.
description: Drop flatbed scans or phone shots; the tool pairs front and back by filename or order, auto-crops and straightens each print, keeps the handwritten back as a linked second image or panel, and lets you type who, where and when once. The caption and approximate date are embedded as standard XMP/IPTC fields so they survive in Google Photos or genealogy software, and everything exports as a ZIP without uploading anything. Aimed at families digitizing albums. Hard to copy only moderately: the moat is a polished client-side crop/deskew/pairing workflow and correct metadata writing, which store-bought phone apps do not combine.
web_delivery: PWA: getUserMedia for phone capture or file drop for flatbed scans, OpenCV.js/WASM or canvas code for crop and deskew, File System Access API / ZIP download for output; no server.
why_hard_to_copy: Client-side image pipeline (edge detection, perspective and page-curve correction) plus correct XMP/IPTC/EXIF writing with partial dates, wrapped in a pairing workflow; a weekend clone would skip the curved-page and metadata correctness.

signals.summary: Wants simple software to scan the front and back of old family photos, paste the back (with the handwriting) onto the same file as the front and add a typed caption underneath.
Looking for a phone app that photographs album and book pages and straightens wavy pages automatically, because proper book scanners are too expensive.
Wants a document-ingest utility that suggests a crop, corrects perspective and wrinkles, cleans shadows and creases, and saves lossless or lossy output for sequences of pages.

competitors_seen.name: Photomyne
competitors_seen.note: Scans photo backs and whole albums but the full feature set needs a paid subscription; app-store only.

competitors_seen.name: Google PhotoScan
competitors_seen.note: Free glare-free phone scans of single prints; Photomyne's own comparison says it has no back-of-photo scanning.

satellite.why_shared: A related photo.SE question about working out a scan's resolution in ppi drew 827 views (2026-06-13), so the audience asks this constantly; pure client-side math.
satellite.handoff: Link: 'Now scan and caption them with BackSide'.

The category is served by Photomyne (paid) and PhotoScan, so differentiation is front+back pairing, standard metadata and no-upload/no-subscription. Be honest that a basic version is a weekend project; the quality of crop/deskew is the real work.

name: Exam Pseudocode Studio
idea: Browser IDE that runs AQA/OCR/Cambridge/IB exam pseudocode, fills the trace table automatically and draws the matching flowchart from the same code.
description: Students and teachers write pseudocode in the exact dialect of their exam board, step through it, and get a trace table generated as it runs plus a flowchart rendered from the same program, so all three exam representations stay consistent. Teachers can share exercises by link. Hard to copy because it needs dialect-accurate parsers and an interpreter for several boards' pseudocode specifications and a flowchart layout that follows exam conventions.
web_delivery: Static SPA on Vercel hobby; parser/interpreter and flowchart layout run in the browser (web worker); Supabase free for shared exercises and class codes.
why_hard_to_copy: Exam-board-specific pseudocode dialects with exact semantics (arrays indexing, string functions, file handling) and exam-style flowchart and trace-table conventions; niche syllabus knowledge most developers lack.

signals.summary: A student wants one tool that combines flowchart, pseudocode and trace-table creation; the tools they tried only do flowcharts and have overwhelming interfaces.

A developer wrote up building an IGCSE pseudocode interpreter, showing hobbyists are attacking the same exam-pseudocode tooling gap (builder-side evidence, not a complaint; predates the window by six days).

name: SheetSalvage
idea: Drag-and-drop tool that salvages data from corrupted .xlsx/.xlsm files entirely in the browser, with nothing uploaded.
description: Reads a damaged OOXML package with a tolerant parser (broken or missing zip directory, malformed sheet XML, lost shared strings), lists which sheets and cells are recoverable and exports a clean workbook or CSVs. Spreadsheets with business data never leave the machine, unlike online repair services. Hard to copy because tolerant zip/XML salvage and handling real-world corruption modes (crash during save, sync conflicts, script damage) needs a corpus of broken files and a lot of edge-case work.
web_delivery: Static site on Vercel hobby; fflate/JSZip-style tolerant unzip plus a custom lenient XML reader in a web worker; no server, no storage.
why_hard_to_copy: Lenient OOXML and zip recovery with a growing corpus of real corruption cases; most clones just call a strict spreadsheet library that fails on damaged files.

signals.summary: Regularly hits corrupted xlsx/xlsm files (scripts, crashes during save, shared-drive conflicts); Excel's Open and Repair often fails or recovers only part, so asks for a free or low-cost tool that recovers sheets, formulas and values, ideally without installing software.

name: Moon & Sun Alignment Finder
idea: Free PWA that tells you the next dates and times the Sun or Moon will sit at a chosen spot in the sky (landmark, skyline notch), including terrain horizon.
description: Pick a location and aim at a landmark (compass or tap on a map/skyline) or enter azimuth and elevation, and get the next several dates when the Moon, full Moon or Sun lines up within a tolerance, plus a yearly sun-path view to judge shade from trees and buildings. Aimed at photographers and gardeners who want it free on Android and iOS. Hard to copy only moderately: ephemeris math is available in libraries, the craft is the reverse search with tolerance, refraction and a terrain horizon profile.
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel hobby: astronomy-engine in the browser, DeviceOrientation/compass for aiming, free public terrain tiles for the horizon, Supabase free for saved spots.
why_hard_to_copy: Reverse ephemeris search with tolerance, refraction and terrain-horizon masking is more work than a sun-position viewer; incumbent apps keep it behind paid mobile apps.

signals.summary: Wants a free or cheap app to point the phone at a spot (for example above a town landmark) and learn the next time the Moon will be there; says known apps only show where the Moon is on a chosen date, not the reverse.

Wants an Android app showing the Sun's position at their location for any week or month to see where light ends up and whether trees or houses shade it, happy to pay once; says existing answers are ten years old.

competitors_seen.note: Paid mobile photo planner with ephemerides and calculators (review page).

name: Rare Sky Events Almanac
idea: Searchable almanac of planetary transits, mutual occultations and eclipses for any observer body over centuries, precomputed and filterable in the browser.
description: Browse or filter long-range lists of transits, occultations and eclipses (Earth and other planets as the viewpoint), with exact timing, visibility by location where relevant and links to compute custom windows in the browser. Aimed at amateur astronomers, science writers and worldbuilders. Hard to copy because it needs validated ephemeris computations cross-checked against published catalogues, but the output is a static dataset that is cheap to host.
web_delivery: Build step precomputes events into static JSON served from Vercel hobby; browser filtering and optional custom search with astronomy-engine in a web worker.
why_hard_to_copy: Domain-expert computation (mutual events seen from other planets, accuracy over centuries) validated against catalogues; not something a generic vibe-coded page can get right.

signals.summary: Asks for a website with long-range lists of transits, eclipses and occultations like an older site that is now gone and only reachable through the web archive.

name: Manuscript Style Linter
idea: Web linter that checks a LaTeX manuscript and bibliography against a chosen journal's style rules and converts US/UK spelling safely.
description: Upload or paste a .tex and .bib, pick a journal rule pack, and get a report with line references for required macros, citation form, title/section/caption capitalization, code markup and missing bib fields such as DOI, plus a spelling normalizer that leaves math, code, quotes and citations untouched. Aimed at researchers whose papers bounce at editorial check. Hard to copy because the value is hand-curated, expert-maintained rule packs and a LaTeX-aware tokenizer, not generic grammar checking.
web_delivery: Client-side TypeScript parser on Vercel hobby; rule packs as JSON in the repo; files never leave the browser; Supabase free only for optional rule-pack contributions.
why_hard_to_copy: Curated per-journal rule packs plus a LaTeX-aware tokenizer that can skip math, verbatim and citations; generic AI or grammar tools do not know journal macros.

signals.summary: Notes that general linters (chktex, lacheck) know nothing about a journal's style guide, so violations are found by editors one revision round at a time, and asks for a tool that checks .tex/.Rnw/.Rmd plus bibliography against the Journal of Statistical Software guide.
A researcher whose target journal requires British English and who is unfamiliar with it asks for a tool to convert the article.

competitors_seen.note: Free LaTeX linter for typography and syntax, not journal-specific.

competitors_seen.name: Paperpal and Writefull
competitors_seen.note: Subscription AI language and submission checks; Overleaf integration but no verified journal-specific rule coverage.

name: Stipend Compass
idea: Crowd-verified atlas of PhD and postdoc stipends by country, university and field, with a living-cost ratio so you can tell if an offer is livable.
description: Prospective and current graduate students look up stipends (reported net amounts, teaching supplements, tuition waivers) and see each one divided by a local living-wage figure, with a 'can I live on this offer' check. name: Luck Tuner
idea: Interactive designer for fair-feeling randomness: compare plain chance, pity counters, pseudo-random distribution and shuffle bags, and get exact streak statistics and code.
description: A game designer enters a target drop or crit chance and sees side by side how independent rolls, pity timers, increasing-chance (PRD) and shuffle-bag systems behave: longest failure streak, expected attempts, variance, and a tunable knob between fully random and fully predictable. The tool solves the constants numerically and exports snippets for common engines. Aimed at indie developers and tabletop designers. Hard to copy because it needs exact Markov-chain analysis and numeric constant solving rather than Monte Carlo guesses.
web_delivery: Static SPA on Vercel hobby; analysis and simulation in a web worker; shareable parameter links; no backend needed.
why_hard_to_copy: Exact Markov-chain streak distributions and numeric PRD constant solving across several systems, with clear visualisation; most posts only hand-wave the math.

signals.summary: A designer wants ways to interpolate between pure random and a deterministic counter so unlucky streaks shrink but outcomes stay unpredictable, with an adjustable amount of randomness.

An indie developer balances weapon and ammo prices against per-wave income using a hand-made spreadsheet and asks how to turn that data into prices; shows the lack of a simple balancing sandbox (adjacent to the RNG need).

name: Fairy Problem Bench

name: Fingerspelling Reader
idea: Installable offline PWA for practising reading fingerspelling (BSL two-handed, Auslan, ASL) at adjustable speed.
description: Learners see words fingerspelled by a clean hand animation at chosen speeds, type what they read, and progress through word lists by level, all cached offline so it works on airgapped phones and planes. Teachers can share word lists by link. Hard to copy only through assets: original, community-reviewed handshape animations for several sign languages are the work, the code is simple.
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel hobby with a service worker caching SVG/animation assets; progress stored locally; Supabase free optional for shared word lists.
why_hard_to_copy: Original handshape assets for multiple sign languages with Deaf-community review; honestly the software is easy, the assets are the moat.

signals.summary: Loves existing HTML fingerspelling-reading games but airgaps home and phone, so asks for an offline desktop or iOS version that practises reading fingerspelling at different speeds; paywalled apps are too risky to try blind.
